findings.title: Provider failure in review is logged as "unexpected error" and no longer re-raised
findings.description: The `except ProviderError` branch used to `raise` into `execute`'s handler. It now calls `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error in step %s", ...)` and returns `_exception_result(...)` directly. A named provider failure is an expected condition, and `dispatch` deliberately logs those at ERROR without a traceback. The new message is misleading and dumps a stack trace for a known failure. The path also skips the handling the re-raise used to reach in `execute`. I can't confirm from the diff that `execute` had no other `ProviderError` handling.

findings.title: Helper called inside the failure handler can raise and hide the original error
findings.description: `effort_sent_by_profile` (in `usage_capture.py`) calls `get_profile`, `ensure_provider_loaded` and `get_provider`. The review action calls it inside the `except ProviderError` block. If any of those lookups fail, the new exception replaces the provider error. The failure artifact and usage record would then be lost, which is the case this block exists to cover. Compute the effort before the `try`, or guard the lookup.

findings.title: Reordered `except ProviderError` in dispatch changes catch precedence
findings.description: `except ProviderError` moved ahead of `except (ModelResolutionError, ModelPoolNotImplemented, KeyError)` and the other specific handlers. Any exception class that also derives from `ProviderError` would now take the generic provider path instead of its specific one. I did not check whether such a class exists. Please confirm there is no subclass relationship, or keep the original order.

findings.title: Fresh pricing-warning set on every review call defeats once-per-alias warning
findings.description: `resolve_cost(alias, ..., set())` is called with a new empty set each time. The pipeline path shares one `UsageCapture` warning set per run, so a run's pipeline-review step and its standalone-style call can warn differently. `UsageCapture` documents WARNING-once-per-alias, but a review-heavy run will repeat the pricing warning. Consider passing the run's set through.

findings.title: Parameter creep and long signatures in one-shot dispatch plumbing
findings.description: `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` gains `max_output_tokens` and `usage_metadata`, and `_one_shot` takes seven positional parameters. The side-channel `usage_metadata` dict (mutated by callee, read by caller via `EFFORT_SENT_KEY`) is implicit coupling. A small result object would be cleaner. `usage_capture.py` also imports `ReviewResult` from the review package into the pipeline layer. This is acceptable but worth watching.

findings.title: Line length likely exceeds the 88-character standard
findings.description: Several new lines look longer than 88 characters. Examples are the `cells = [step, row.action_type, _model_cell(record), ...]` line in `stats_views.py`, the `_one_shot(...)` call in `dispatch.py`, and the `unrecorded` property in `usage_report.py`. The project may configure a wider limit in `pyproject.toml`; I couldn't check. Run `ruff format` and `ruff check`.

findings.title: Test coverage is strong
Stats reviews reports a missing directory as exit 0 on stdout
findings.description: With `--json`, a missing review directory prints a plain-text message instead of JSON. Scripted consumers would fail to parse it. This is minor but worth deciding on explicitly.
